column1: # Exit-residue ratchet baseline (RFC-0114 §25; restored on the wasm route by
# RFC-0125 §3 M4). One row per example the route builds:
# clean: exits its own code with zero residue under an audited build.
# leak N: at most N blocks of residue. other: exits nonzero by design and the
# audit stays quiet. An example with no row must come out clean; shrinking a
# leak row is the ratchet turning, and it only turns one way.
# A program that does not build is not a row: `route.rs`'s three lists
# (KNOWN_DIVERGENT, EXPECTED_CHECK_FAILURE, WASM_ONLY) own that question, and

# the capture a source mints, and the value `?` copies — so every leak from
# here is a regression and a red gate, which is the only state this column is
